req.title: Delete only by author
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden when a user attempts to delete a post they did not author.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-020 requires HTTP 403 when a non-author attempts to delete a post. The violation was test[4] (test_post_survives_failed_403_delete_attempt) which had kind=negative but heuristic=STC. STC (State Transition Coverage) is a structural/positive heuristic; a negative kind test must use NEG, EP, BVA, or DT. Fix: change heuristic from STC to NEG, which is correct because the test exercises the error pathway (403 leaves state unchanged) — a negative scenario verifying no side-effects. All other tests are preserved exactly as before.

tests.name: test_author_can_delete_own_post
preconditions: Database contains post id=2 authored by user id=1 (Rahul)
expected: Post id=2 no longer accessible (GET /2/update returns 404)
trace: R-FLASKR-020 positive path: author deletes own post
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_author_can_delete_own_post():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.test_client() as client:
        with app.app_context():
            from flaskr.db import init_db
            init_db()
        r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
        assert r.status_code == 302
        r = client.post('/2/delete')
        assert r.status_code == 302
        assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
        r = client.get('/2/update')
        assert r.status_code == 404

test_author_can_delete_own_post()

def test_unauthenticated_delete_redirects_not_403():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.test_client() as client:

        assert r.status_code == 302
        assert r.status_code != 403
        assert r.status_code != 200

tests.name: test_post_survives_failed_403_delete_attempt
preconditions: Post id=7 authored by Anjali (id=2) exists
actions: Log out, log in as Anjali
GET /7/update to confirm post still exists
expected: Post id=7 still exists after the failed attempt (GET /7/update returns 200)
trace: R-FLASKR-020 negative: 403 must leave system state unchanged — non-author delete has no side-effects
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_post_survives_failed_403_delete_attempt():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.test_client() as client:
        with app.app_context():
            from flaskr.db import init_db
            init_db()
        client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
        r = client.post('/7/delete')
        assert r.status_code == 403
        client.get('/auth/logout')
        client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
        r = client.get('/7/update')
        assert r.status_code == 200

test_post_survives_failed_403_delete_attempt()

preconditions: Post id=1 authored by James (id=5) exists
Ishaan (id=3) is logged in — not the author
expected: HTTP 403 exactly — not 404, not 302, not 200, not 400
